newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-AFRICAN COUNTRIES TO BID FOR 2006 WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICAN COUNTRIES TO BID FOR 2006 WORLD CUP.

text.p: Egypt, Morocco and South Africa hope to bring the World Cup finals to the African continent for the first time in 2006.
FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said on Friday that the countries were interested in making bids.
They will face fierce European opposition from 1974 hosts Germany and 1966 organisers England, whose chances of staging the finals may have been boosted by the success of Euro 96.
Argentina and Brazil have also announced they will bid.
Speaking at a symposium in Munich, Blatter also said he might be ready to continue in his position at FIFA after 1998, his expected retirement year.
"Everything depends on who becomes the new president. If he thinks I can still be useful I will stay --- even if my role is changed," Blatter said.
